directories.noScanTitle: Webhook-eligible only — scanner and watcher skip this directory. Useful for an NZBGet/SABnzbd downloads landing zone.

video.title: Video Settings
video.redetectTitle: Re-detect hardware encoders. Use this after enabling /dev/dri passthrough or changing the BIOS iGPU setting.

encoderHelp.nvenc: Hardware encoding using your NVIDIA GPU. Fast, lower power usage. Slightly larger files than CPU at the same quality.
encoderHelp.qsv: Hardware encoding using Intel Quick Sync (Gen8+ iGPUs through Arc / Battlemage). Fast and very power-efficient. Requires /dev/dri passthrough — see the help block below.
encoderHelp.vaapi: Hardware encoding via VA-API. Works on Intel iGPUs and AMD GPUs (Polaris / Vega / RDNA). Driver-quality varies; use QSV instead on Intel where available. Requires /dev/dri passthrough.
encoderHelp.libx265: Software encoding using CPU. Slower but achieves better compression per bitrate.

passthrough.findGid: Find the GID with stat -c '%g' /dev/dri/renderD128 on the host.
passthrough.restart: Then docker compose down && up -d and click Re-detect above.
passthrough.verify: Run docker exec shrinkerr vainfo to verify the encoder profiles your hardware exposes.

video.parallelJobsHelp: Number of simultaneous encoding jobs. Higher = faster queue processing but more GPU/CPU load.
video.ffmpegThreadsHelp: auto (0) lets ffmpeg use every available core per job — fine for a single job, but with Parallel Jobs > 1 two jobs on an 8-core CPU each try to use all 8 cores and fight each other, eroding throughput. 1–2 is a good cap for older CPUs running parallel software (libx265) encodes. NVENC / QSV / VAAPI users can usually leave this at 1–2 too — the GPU does the heavy lifting, ffmpeg just needs threads for muxing and filtering. Set higher if you want a single job to fully saturate a modern many-core CPU.
video.convertFromHelp: Select which source codecs should be converted to the target codec.
video.vmafDecoderWarning: ⚠ VMAF won't run on jobs that use this decoder. See the VMAF section.

nvdec.label: Use NVDEC for decode
nvdec.help: Decodes the source on the GPU before NVENC encodes it. Frames stay on-device — no PCIe transfer. Falls back silently to software decode for unsupported source codecs (MS-MPEG4v3, exotic formats).
nvdec.notDetected: NVDEC not detected on this host.

bitDepth.label: Bit Depth
bitDepth.help: 10-bit is best for quality (less banding, slightly larger files on most sources) but requires Pascal-or-newer NVIDIA (GTX 10xx / Quadro P-series / RTX). 8-bit is the only option for Maxwell silicon (GTX 9xx / 750 Ti / Quadro M-series), produces smaller files on most material, and encodes a little faster. Match source uses 10-bit only when the source is already 10-bit, otherwise 8-bit — avoids the upconvert overhead when the input doesn't benefit from it.

video.nvencCqHelp: Controls quality vs file size. Lower = higher quality, larger files. 18-20: Transparent quality (recommended). 21-24: Good quality, noticeable savings. 25+: Visible quality loss, maximum compression.

cpuFallback.title: CPU fallback
cpuFallback.help: When an NVENC job is picked up by a CPU-only worker, use these libx265 settings instead of auto-translating from the NVENC preset/CQ. Leave blank for automatic translation.

gpuFallback.title: GPU fallback
gpuFallback.help: When a libx265 job is picked up by a GPU-capable worker, use these NVENC settings instead of the hardcoded defaults. Leave blank for automatic.

x265Nvdec.label: Use NVDEC for decode (mixed mode)
x265Nvdec.help: Decodes the source on NVIDIA GPU (NVDEC), then transfers frames to CPU for libx265 encoding. Net win on slow CPUs paired with a dGPU; on modern CPUs the PCIe transfer overhead usually exceeds the savings. Falls back silently to software decode for unsupported source codecs. Defaults off.

video.cpuPresetHelp: Controls encoding speed vs compression efficiency. Slower presets produce smaller files at the same quality. medium: Balanced speed and quality (recommended). slow/slower: Better compression, significantly slower. fast/veryfast: Quick encodes, larger files.
video.crfHelp: Controls quality vs file size. Lower = higher quality, larger files. CRF 18-20 is typically transparent to the original.

qsvDecode.label: Use QSV for decode
qsvDecode.help: Decodes the source on the Intel iGPU before QSV encodes it. Frames stay on-die — no upload overhead. Falls back silently to software decode for unsupported source codecs.
qsvDecode.notDetected: QSV decode not detected on this host.

video.qsvPresetHelp: Encoder analysis depth. Note: unlike libx265, QSV's preset cost curve is nearly flat — `slower` is typically only ~10-20% slower than `medium` with modest quality gains. The bigger lever for QSV quality is the look-ahead toggle below. medium is fine for most hardware.
video.qsvQualityHelp: QSV's ICQ-mode quality target. Lower = higher quality, larger files. 20-22 is typically transparent; 23-26 is good quality with noticeable savings. Rough cross-encoder mapping: QSV CQ ≈ NVENC CQ (within ±1) ≈ libx265 CRF + 1.

lookahead.label: Look-ahead rate control
lookahead.help: Trades ~10–20% encode speed for a small visual quality bump on rapid-motion scenes. Useful when the hardware has throughput to spare (Arc / 11th-gen+); diminishing returns on older Intel iGPUs.

vaapiDecode.label: Use VAAPI for decode
vaapiDecode.help: Decodes the source on the GPU/iGPU via VAAPI before encoding. Frames stay on the DRM device. Falls back silently to software decode for unsupported source codecs.
vaapiDecode.notDetected: VAAPI decode not detected on this host.

video.vaapiCompressionHelp: Driver-side analysis depth, 0–7. Semantics vary by driver (Mesa AMD vs Intel iHD), but lower values consistently produce smaller files at the cost of speed. 4 is a sane median. On Intel hardware where both VAAPI and QSV work, QSV usually produces better quality per bit at similar throughput — VAAPI is most useful on AMD GPUs (where QSV isn't an option).
video.vaapiQpHelp: Constant quantizer (CQP) target. Lower = higher quality, larger files. 20-22 is typically transparent; 23-26 trades quality for size sensibly.

smart.title: Smart Encoding
smart.contentTypeHelp: Automatically detects content type from filenames (anime, grain, animation, remux) and applies optimized CQ values. Anime compresses well (CQ 22), grain needs conservative settings (CQ 24). Applied when no encoding rule sets a CQ value.
smart.hwWarning_one: ⚠ VMAF will not run on hardware-decoded jobs. VMAF compares the encoded output to software-decoded source frames. With {{count}} hardware decode toggle currently on ({{decoders}}), jobs that use those encoders will skip VMAF — no score is computed and the quality threshold won't be applied. To enforce VMAF on every job, disable the hardware decode toggles in the encoder section above.
smart.hwWarning_other: ⚠ VMAF will not run on hardware-decoded jobs. VMAF compares the encoded output to software-decoded source frames. With {{count}} hardware decode toggles currently on ({{decoders}}), jobs that use those encoders will skip VMAF — no score is computed and the quality threshold won't be applied. To enforce VMAF on every job, disable the hardware decode toggles in the encoder section above.
smart.vmafHelp: VMAF (Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion) is a perceptual video quality metric developed by Netflix. It scores encoded video from 0-100 by comparing it against the original source, predicting how a human viewer would rate the quality. When enabled, Shrinkerr runs a frame-accurate VMAF comparison between the original and encoded file after conversion. Shrinkerr only analyses a 30-second sample window (centred at ~33% into the file), not the whole encode — so this typically adds well under a minute per job on a modern GPU, and gives you confidence that your CQ settings produce acceptable quality.
smart.minScore: Reject encodes below a minimum VMAF score
smart.minScoreHelp: When enabled, any encode whose measured VMAF score is below the threshold is discarded — the encoded temp file is deleted, the original is left in place, and the job is recorded as rejected with the score and threshold visible in the job details. Useful as a safety net against overly-aggressive CQ/CRF settings.
smart.resAwareHelp: Use different CQ values per resolution. 4K benefits from higher CQ since downsampling during playback hides artifacts. Fallback when no rule or content detection sets CQ.

vmafRemeasure.title: Re-measure suspect VMAF scores
vmafRemeasure.help: Re-runs VMAF on completed jobs whose recorded score landed below "Excellent" or got flagged measurement-suspect (libvmaf can de-sync mid-window and return artificially low scores on visually-fine encodes). Skips jobs where the original pre-rename file no longer exists. Uses the same bimodal-aware retry path as fresh encodes.
vmafRemeasure.noCandidates: No candidates — every completed job is at "Excellent" or has no comparable source.

nvencPresets.title: NVENC presets (GPU)
nvencPresets.desc: Higher preset = slower encoding but better compression. Unlike libx265, NVENC preset speed changes very little between p1 and p7 — the quality gains are also modest. Default to p3-p5 and adjust CQ for size.
nvencPresets.note: Speeds are approximate for 1080p on Quadro P2200.

x265Presets.title: libx265 presets (CPU)
x265Presets.desc: libx265 preset cost scales EXPONENTIALLY — each step right roughly doubles encode time. Default `medium` is the quality-per-minute sweet spot; drop to `fast` or `veryfast` for backfills, bump to `slow`/`slower` only for archival masters.
x265Presets.note: Speeds are rough for 10-bit output on a modern desktop CPU. M1/M2 Macs run ~40-60% of these numbers; older CPUs slower.

cqCrf.title: Understanding CQ / CRF
cqCrf.desc: CQ (NVENC) and CRF (libx265) control the quality target. Lower = higher quality, larger files. The encoder allocates more bits to complex scenes and fewer to simple ones.

tips.sources: Sources: Blu-ray rips (15-40 GB) see the biggest savings; WEB-DL files (3-8 GB) are already well-compressed — expect smaller gains, or bump CQ/CRF 2-3 points.
tips.grain: Grain-heavy content (film, older movies) needs lower CQ/CRF values to preserve detail, or the encoder smears grain into blocks.
tips.animation: Animation compresses extremely well — even CQ 25+ looks great. Consider a dedicated rule targeting your anime directory.
tips.nvencVsX265: NVENC vs libx265 quality: NVENC CQ ≈ libx265 CRF + 0–2 for matched perceptual quality. libx265 still produces ~25% smaller files at the same quality, trading 5-50× encode time.
tips.x265Scaling: libx265 preset scaling: each step slower roughly doubles encode time. Going from `fast` to `slow` is 4×, `fast` to `veryslow` is 20×+. Know your patience budget before picking.
tips.nvencScaling: NVENC preset scaling: minimal — p7 is only ~5× slower than p1 on the same card, and the quality gap is small. Default p3-p5 is usually the right answer.
tips.testEncode: Try a test encode first: the Estimate modal's Test encode button runs a 30s clip through your chosen settings and reports the VMAF score. Cheaper than starting a 20-minute job on a bad preset.
tips.mixedFleets: Mixed fleets: if a remote worker has only the other encoder, the NVENC↔libx265 translation maps presets/quality over — see Nodes → Settings for the exact mapping, or pin a fallback preset/quality in the CPU/GPU fallback fields above.

current.greatQuality: Great quality with good space savings

audio.title: Audio Settings
audio.alwaysKeepHelp: Audio tracks in these languages are kept by default. You can override per-track in the file detail editor.

dedup.label: Keep only the best track per always-keep language
dedup.help: When a file has multiple tracks in the same always-keep language (e.g. EAC3 5.1 + AAC 2.0 + commentary, all English), keep only the highest-quality one by default (ranked by channels, then codec: TrueHD > FLAC/PCM > DTS-HD MA > DTS > EAC3 > AC3 > AAC). Turn off to keep every track in always-keep languages — you can still uncheck individual tracks in the file detail editor.

keepNative.label: Auto-keep native language audio tracks
keepNative.help: Automatically keep audio tracks matching each file's detected native language. Disable if you only want to keep dubbed / specified language tracks. (Subtitles have their own toggle in the Subtitles section — they're off by default.)

reorderNative.label: Reorder native language to first audio stream
reorderNative.help: During conversion or audio cleanup, move native-language audio tracks to the first position so they become the default playback stream. Files where native isn't first will be tagged for audio cleanup.

keepUnknown.label: Keep unknown/undefined tracks
keepUnknown.help: Tracks tagged as "und" or with no language metadata

autoDetect.label: Auto-detect languages for unknown tracks before converting
autoDetect.help: Before converting or cleaning up audio, run language detection on "und"/unknown audio and text-subtitle tracks so keep/remove rules use real languages. You can also run detection manually per file from the file detail view.

model.label: Audio detection model
model.medium: Medium — higher accuracy, ~1.5 GB, GPU recommended
model.large-v3: Large-v3 — best accuracy (incl. low-resource langs), ~3 GB, GPU strongly recommended
model.help: faster-whisper model for spoken-language ID. Larger is more accurate on non-English speech at the cost of download size, RAM, and speed. Medium/Large-v3 are practical only with an NVIDIA GPU (the :nvenc image). Downloads on first use; takes effect on the next detection (no restart).

audio.confidenceHelp: Minimum confidence (0–1) to accept a detected language — lower tags more tracks but risks wrong tags. Defaults: audio 0.6, subtitle 0.7. (A SHRINKERR_* env var, if set, overrides these.)

conversion.title: Audio Conversion
conversion.bitrateHelp: Higher bitrate = better audio quality, larger files. 128 kbps: Good for stereo. 256 kbps: Good for 5.1 surround. 384-640 kbps: High quality surround.
conversion.downmixHelp: Convert 5.1/7.1 surround to stereo. Saves space but loses surround channels.

lossless.label: Auto-convert lossless audio
lossless.help: Automatically convert lossless audio tracks (DTS-HD MA, TrueHD, PCM, FLAC) to a smaller lossy codec during video conversion. Lossy tracks are left untouched.

removing.title: Space Saved by Removing Tracks
removing.desc: Each extra audio track adds significant file size. A 2-hour movie with 4 unnecessary audio tracks can waste 1-8 GB.

tips.copy: Use "Copy" mode unless you specifically need a different codec — it's instant and lossless
tips.bluray: Blu-ray discs often include 3-6 language dubs — removing them is the easiest space win
tips.lossless: DTS-HD MA and TrueHD are lossless and huge — consider keeping only for your primary language
tips.commentary: Commentary tracks are usually AC3 stereo (~250 MB each) — safe to remove unless you listen to them
tips.native: The native language is auto-detected per file, so foreign films keep their original audio

current.onlyNative: Only the native language track is kept
current.keptCount_one: {{count}} language kept by default, plus native auto-detected per file
current.keptCount_other: {{count}} languages kept by default, plus native auto-detected per file

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.keepHelp: Internal subtitle tracks in these languages will always be kept. Forced subtitles are always kept regardless of language. Only tracks in other languages will be marked for removal.

keepUnknown.label: Keep unknown/undefined subtitles
keepUnknown.help: Subtitle tracks tagged as "und" or with no language metadata

keepNative.label: Auto-keep native language subtitle tracks
keepNative.help: Keep subtitle tracks whose language matches the file's detected native language, even if it's not in the keep list above. Defaults off — for most setups, native-language subs on a same-language audio track are noise. Turn on if you want them for SDH / hearing-impaired reasons.

autoDetect.label: Auto-detect languages for unknown tracks before converting
autoDetect.help: Before converting or cleaning up subtitles, run language detection on "und"/unknown audio and text-subtitle tracks so keep/remove rules use real languages. This is the same setting as in the Audio section. You can also run detection manually per file from the file detail view.

external.title: External Subtitles
external.mergeHelp: During conversion or remux, embed external .srt, .ass, .ssa, .sub, .vtt files found alongside the video into the MKV container. Language is detected from the filename (e.g. .eng.srt, .en.forced.srt).
external.deleteAfter: Delete external subtitle files after merge
external.deleteWarning: The original .srt/.ass files will be permanently deleted after a successful merge.

p1.label: Fastest
p1.desc: Lowest quality, highest speed. Good for quick tests.

p2.label: Very Fast
p2.desc: Slightly better quality than p1, still very quick.

p3.label: Fast
p3.desc: Reasonable quality with good speed. Good for batch processing.

p4.label: Medium
p4.desc: Balanced quality and speed. Good default for general use.

p6.label: Very Slow
p6.desc: High quality with good compression. Recommended for storage.

p7.label: Slowest
p7.desc: Best compression NVENC offers (best quality-per-bit → smaller files at the same CQ). Slowest speed.

hevc.label: HEVC / H.265
hevc.desc: Modern codec, excellent compression. Widely supported.

av1.label: AV1 (future)
av1.desc: Next-gen codec, best compression. Requires AV1-capable GPU.

copy.label: Copy (no re-encode)
copy.desc: Keep original audio codec. Fastest, no quality loss.

aac.label: AAC
aac.desc: Widely compatible. Good quality at lower bitrates.

eac3.label: EAC3 (Dolby Digital+)
eac3.desc: Enhanced AC3. Better quality at same bitrate.

opus.label: Opus
opus.desc: Best quality per bitrate. Limited device support.

flac.label: FLAC
flac.desc: Lossless compression. Large files, perfect quality.

copy.label: Copy (keep original)
copy.desc: Keep the original resolution. No scaling applied.

1080p.label: 1080p (1920×1080)
1080p.desc: Full HD. Good balance of quality and size for most content.

720p.label: 720p (1280×720)
720p.desc: HD. Significant size reduction, still good on smaller screens.

480p.label: 480p (854×480)
480p.desc: SD. Very small files. Best for mobile or low-bandwidth.
